subject: Private K8s onboarding playbook & readiness checklist — NexaHealth
body:
Message 1/4
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@nexahealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: NexaHealth EngOps <engops@nexahealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private cluster kickoff & high-level constraints

Markus / team,

Thanks again for the intro call earlier this week. We're moving toward a private (on-prem) deployment for our inference workloads and want to lock down a practical onboarding plan. High-level constraints from our side:

- Two datacenters (primary + DR) with cross-site dark fiber; no public IPs on node hosts.
- Air-gapped-ish policy: egress only via an approved NAT host and proxy; images must come from our private registry.
- Mix of CPU workload (control plane, pre/post-processing) and GPU inference (NVIDIA A100 at 80GB).
- Storage tiers: hot NVMe for model shards, large SATA/SSD for logs/artifacts, object storage accessible via S3 gateway.
- Compliance: SOC2-ready, must be able to provide audit logs and KMS integration.

We'd like Redwood to provide a short checklist for cluster readiness (node sizing, PV guidance, CSI choices, network ports, egress plan) so our infra team can provision before the architecture review. Also attaching our rough storage profile.

Can you send a compact playbook we can use as a provisioning checklist?

—Jordan
Jordan Ellis
EngOps Lead, NexaHealth
j.ellis@nexahealth.com

---

Message 2/4
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private cluster kickoff & high-level constraints

Jordan — thanks for the clear constraints. Attached is a concise onboarding playbook (PDF) and a short checklist you can hand to the provisioning team. Key points up front (summary):

1) Cluster topology
   - 3 control-plane VMs per AZ in primary site (k8s HA). Control plane may be split across sites for DR but we'll plan for control-plane failover via external etcd or managed etcd operator.
   - Worker node pools:
       * infra-nodes: 3-5 VMs, 8 vCPU / 32GB, for logging/storage controller, LB, ingress.
       * compute-cpu: sized to pre/post-processing, 16 vCPU / 64GB.
       * gpu-infer: 1:1 mapping to GPUs. For A100-80GB, recommend node instance with 80GB device and 256GB system RAM. Start with 4 GPU nodes for initial capacity (autoscale up).

2) Storage guidance
   - Use Rook/Ceph (RBD) for block-backed PVs for model shards — gives replication across OSDs and snapshots.
   - Local NVMe for ephemeral cache (kubelet root+local-provisioner) to accelerate KV/cache reads.
   - For large model artifacts and long-term artifacts, use S3 gateway (on-prem MinIO or object-store) mounted by the app layer; avoid putting models directly on NFS.
   - Recommended PV classes: "fast-ssd-rbd" (replicated RBD, 3 replicas, encryption-at-rest), "bulk-hdd" (for logs, lower IOPS).

3) CSI & backups
   - CSI: use Rook/Ceph CSI. Keep driver at supported semver aligned with k8s version.
   - Snapshot policy via VolumeSnapshot + Velero for cluster-level backups to S3 gateway. Schedule daily model snapshots pre-deploy.

4) Networking
   - Calico in policy-only mode with IPIP disabled (use routing mode) unless you need overlay tunnels.
   - MetalLB in BGP mode where available; fallback to layer-2 in an isolated VLAN.
   - Egress NAT through dedicated gateway(s) with firewall rules restricting outbound to Redwood endpoints for control-plane callbacks.
   - Pod CIDR: reserve /16 per site; Node allocatable: plan for 110 pods/node to avoid ENI-like constraints.

5) Security & compliance
   - KMS integration: we support KMS wraps via Vault HSM or HSM-backed KMS; we will propose an EKM flow for key rotation and envelope encryption.
   - Audit collection: Fluentd -> object-store with lifecycle; retain logs per your policy.
   - RBAC: enforce PodSecurityPolicies or OPA Gatekeeper policies for allowed images and seccomp profiles.

6) Operational runbook items (short checklist)
   - Confirm image registry access (credentials + proxy allowlist).
   - Ensure time sync (chrony/ntpd) across nodes.
   - Provide GPU driver + CUDA compatible node images; test kubelet eviction thresholds with stress test.
   - Provide network ACLs for these ports: 6443 (API server), etcd ports (2379/2380) between control-plane nodes, 10250 kubelet, 9000 (object-store), BGP ports if MetalLB BGP.

I've included a single-page checklist in the PDF and a recommended node sizing table. Priyom — raising a couple of questions inline below about storage IO and CSI choices for Nexa's particular profile.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-private-onprem-checklist.pdf (1 page)

Message 3/4 (internal)
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster kickoff & high-level constraints

Markus — quick technical notes to add to the playbook (copied into the PDF in v2):

- For high-throughput model shards we should recommend NVMe-backed OSDs and set ceph pool crush rules to prefer local NVMe OSDs; recommend 3x replication minimum for production.
- If Nexa's traffic profile is heavy on small random reads (KV-cache-like), propose using bluestore tuning: target prefetch=false, osd_op_threads=16, and set filestore/wal on separate devices only if using filestore (we don't).
- Rook/Ceph operator versions: call out the tested combo (ceph-17.x + rook-1.9) and the k8s supported matrix (1.22–1.26) — we'll provide exact matrix in doc.
- For snapshot speed, use thick-provisioned RBD for model checkpoints; snapshots are cheap but restores require network IO planning. Test restore time with a 100GB shard.
- Recommend node disk layout for GPU nodes: 1x 2TB NVMe for model working set (fast-ssd-rbd OSDs), 1x 6TB SATA for local logs/artifacts (bulk-hdd).

I'll update the checklist and include a short test plan (restore time, eviction under mem pressure, network e2e). Also, we should call out the required kernel modules and MIG/SMI settings for A100s.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Cc: NexaHealth EngOps <engops@nexahealth.com>, Aaron Patel <aaron@procurement.nexahealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster kickoff & high-level constraints

Team — this is excellent, thank you. A couple of follow-ups:

- Procurement needs a node BOM and rough OPEX/CapEx estimate. Aaron, can you coordinate with Markus for a cost snapshot (we just need order-of-magnitude for current pilot).
- Ops will provision the control plane and networking this week. Markus — can you and Priyom join a 60-minute architecture review Thursday 09:00 PT to walk the playbook and the test plan? We'll invite the storage vendor as well.
- We have two items to confirm on Nexa side: HSM availability for KMS and whether MinIO will be set up in front of our object store. We'll update the storage profile spreadsheet (attached).

If you can drop the revised checklist (PDF v2) and the small node-sizing CSV into the shared Drive link, we'll mark the readiness tasks as complete.

Thanks — Jordan

Attachments: nexa-storage-profile.xlsx
